The evidence presented in the text is of low credibility regarding its substantive value to the legal matter. While the financial statements are relevant to the claim of discrepancies in reported earnings, their status as photocopies without original copies for verification significantly undermines their admissibility and weight. In legal proceedings, the best evidence rule often requires original documents to prove their contents, and the bank's contestation of authenticity further weakens the plaintiff's position. Without the originals, the court may exclude the documents or give them little to no probative value.
